title: From hearing to speaking
made: 2026-11-25, written by Claude for week 2 from his week-1 summary (7/7 lessons, 90% accuracy, felt about right) and his conversation-practice error patterns
focus: More speaking: base form after gusto/kailangan, pronouns in second place (hindi ako, palagi kaming) and kasama/numbers with na, his top conversation mistakes, plus last week's missed lines brought back.

lessons.title: Gusto kong... (want to, need to)
lessons.intro: Your top mix-up in conversation practice: 'Gusto kong binili' instead of 'Gusto kong bumili'. After gusto, ayaw, kailangan and puwede the verb stays in its plain base form, because the time is already in 'gusto'. This lesson drills it with things you really say at home.

words.en: Can we ...? / Is it okay to ...?
I don't want any more / I've had enough.

dialogue.tl: Ano ang gusto mong gawin ngayong araw?
dialogue.en: What do you want to do today?

dialogue.tl: Gusto kong magpahinga. Pagod ako.
dialogue.en: I want to rest. I'm tired.

dialogue.tl: Sige. Pero kailangan nating bumili ng gatas.
dialogue.en: Okay. But we need to buy milk.

dialogue.tl: Puwede bang mamaya na lang?
Sige, mamaya na lang. Matulog ka muna.

grammar.title: Base form after gusto, ayaw, kailangan, puwede
grammar.explain: Gusto, ayaw, kailangan and puwede already carry the time, so the verb after them has no time of its own: like English 'want to buy', not 'want bought'. The base form: -um- verbs look like the done form (kumain, bumili, lumabas); mag- verbs keep mag- (maglaro, mag-aral, not nag-); ma- verbs keep ma- (matulog, maligo). Add the linker -ng to the word before the verb: gusto ko + ng = gusto kong, kailangan ko + ng = kailangan kong, ayoko + ng = ayokong. 'Binili' is wrong twice here: it has a time (done) and it is object focus.

lessons.culture: With your mother-in-law, start a request with 'Puwede po bang...?' (Is it okay if...?). It sounds gentle and respectful, and it uses the same base-form rule: 'Puwede po bang magpahinga muna ako?' (Is it okay if I rest first?).

accept: gusto kong mag aral ng tagalog
gusto ko talagang mag-aral ng tagalog

exercises.prompt: At the table, you're done eating: 'I don't want any more.'

accept: kailangan ko pong bumili ng gatas

exercises.prompt: Is it okay if I rest first? (to an elder)
exercises.answer: Puwede po bang magpahinga muna ako?

lessons.title: Short words go second
lessons.intro: In practice you said 'Palagi naglalaro kami' and 'Walang confidence ako'. Tagalog pulls short pronouns (ako, ka, siya, kami, ko, mo) up to second place, right after the first word. Last week 'Why is she crying?' tripped you up for the same reason.

dialogue.tl: Bakit siya umiiyak?
Hindi ko po alam. Baka gutom na po siya.
dialogue.en: I don't know. Maybe she's hungry.

dialogue.tl: Kumain na ba siya?
Hindi pa po siya kumakain.
Ay, kaya pala. Pakainin mo na siya.
dialogue.en: Oh, that's why. Feed her now.

grammar.title: Pronouns in second place
grammar.explain: Short pronouns (ako, ka, siya, kami, tayo, sila, ko, mo, niya) and little words like na, pa, ba, po come right after the FIRST word of the sentence, even when that word is hindi, palagi, wala, bakit or baka. So: 'Hindi ako pagod', not 'Hindi pagod ako'. When the pronoun lands in front of a verb or noun after palagi or wala, it takes the linker -ng: kami becomes kaming, ako becomes akong.

lessons.culture: When a baby cries, relatives start guessing out loud: 'Baka gutom' (maybe hungry), 'Baka inaantok' (maybe sleepy). Joining the guessing in Tagalog is an easy way into the conversation with Lola.

lessons.title: When you don't understand
lessons.intro: Lola lives with you, so you get Tagalog practice every day. These lines keep a conversation going when she talks too fast or uses a word you don't know, so you don't have to switch to English.

words.tl: Ano po ang ibig sabihin ng ...?
Paano po sabihin ang ... sa Tagalog?
words.en: How do you say ... in Tagalog?

dialogue.tl: Pakikuha mo nga ang bote sa kusina.
dialogue.en: Please get the bottle from the kitchen.

dialogue.tl: Paki-ulit po. Dahan-dahan lang po.
dialogue.en: Please say it again. Slowly, please.

dialogue.tl: Kunin mo ang bote. Sa kusina.
dialogue.en: Get the bottle. In the kitchen.

dialogue.tl: Ah, opo! Naiintindihan ko po.
Magaling ka na, ah!
Salamat po. Nag-aaral pa po ako.

grammar.title: Paki- means please
grammar.explain: Put paki- in front of a verb root to ask nicely: ulit (again) becomes paki-ulit, abot (pass) becomes pakiabot, kuha (get) becomes pakikuha, sara (close) becomes pakisara. Add po for elders. The hyphen is only there before a vowel (paki-ulit); you'll also see it written pakiulit.

lessons.culture: Filipino relatives often switch to English to be kind. If you want her to stay in Tagalog, say: 'Sa Tagalog po, para matuto ako.' (In Tagalog, please, so I can learn.) Most Lolas are delighted to become the teacher.

exercises.prompt: Your mother-in-law is talking too fast. You say:
Please say it again. (to an elder)
Ask an elder how to say 'bottle' in Tagalog.
exercises.answer: Paano po sabihin ang bottle sa Tagalog?
accept: paano po sabihin ang bottle sa tagalog
paano po sasabihin ang bottle sa tagalog
paano po sabihin sa tagalog ang bottle
ano po ang bottle sa tagalog
ano po sa tagalog ang bottle

exercises.prompt: In Tagalog, please, so I can learn. (to an elder)
exercises.answer: Sa Tagalog po, para matuto ako.

lessons.title: Every day with the baby
lessons.intro: One verb form covers both 'is doing right now' and 'does every day'. Last week 'I'm eating now' and 'The baby is drinking milk' were misses, so they're back here alongside the baby's daily routine.

words.en: changes a diaper / is changing a diaper

dialogue.tl: Anong oras gumigising si {child}?
Maaga po. Alas-sais po.
Tapos, ano ang ginagawa ninyo?
dialogue.en: Then what do you two do?

dialogue.tl: Umiinom po siya ng gatas, tapos naglalaro kami.
dialogue.en: She drinks her milk, then we play.

dialogue.tl: Naliligo ba siya araw-araw?
dialogue.en: Does she have a bath every day?

dialogue.tl: Opo, tuwing umaga po.

grammar.title: Now and every day: the ongoing form
grammar.explain: The ongoing form means both 'is doing now' and 'does regularly'. To make it, repeat the first syllable of the root. -um- verbs: kain becomes kumakain, inom becomes umiinom, gising becomes gumigising. mag- verbs change to nag-: laro becomes naglalaro, palit becomes nagpapalit. ma- verbs change to na-: tulog becomes natutulog, ligo becomes naliligo. Add ngayon (now) or araw-araw / tuwing ... (every ...) to make it clear.

lessons.culture: Clock times use Spanish-based numbers with alas-: alas-sais (6:00), alas-siyete (7:00), alas-otso (8:00). Tagalog numbers (isa, dalawa...) are for counting things. So it's 'alas-dos' for 2:00 but 'dalawang bote' for two bottles.

exercises.prompt: We play every day: Araw-araw kaming ___.

options: She has a bath every morning.
She had a bath this morning.
exercises.answer: She has a bath every morning.

exercises.prompt: The baby is eating a banana.

options: Umiinom ang kape ni Lola tuwing umaga.
Umiinom ng kape si Lola tuwing umaga.
Umiinom ng kape ni Lola tuwing umaga.
Iinom ng kape si Lola tuwing umaga.
exercises.answer: Umiinom ng kape si Lola tuwing umaga.

lessons.title: Kasama: who's with you
lessons.intro: 'Nagkasama ako si Kuya' and 'mag-kasama kami' came up three times in practice. Kasama isn't a verb; it means 'companion / together with'. Here's how to say who you're with and who lives with you, plus the in-law words.

words.tl: Nakatira sa amin ang biyenan ko.

dialogue.tl: Sino ang kasama mo sa bahay?
Kasama ko po ang asawa ko at si {child}.
Nakatira pa ba sa inyo ang nanay niya?
dialogue.en: Is her mother still living with you?

dialogue.tl: Opo, nakatira po sa amin ang biyenan ko.
dialogue.en: Yes, my mother-in-law lives with us.

dialogue.tl: Mabuti naman, may tumutulong sa iyo.
Opo. Pero ako ang kasama ni {child} buong araw.
dialogue.en: Yes. But I'm the one with {child} all day.

grammar.title: Kasama ko si ... (not nagkasama ako)
grammar.explain: Kasama works like a noun: 'my companion'. So the person who is with you takes si/ang, and you take a ng-pronoun: 'Kasama ko si Kuya' (Kuya is with me). Don't add nag-/mag- and don't use ako. For '... and I' say 'kami ni ...': 'Kami ni Kuya ang pumunta.' For someone living with you, use nakatira: 'Nakatira sa amin ...' (lives with us).

examples.en: Kuya and I were the ones who went.

examples.tl: Nakatira sa amin ang nanay niya.

lessons.culture: The in-law words are biyenan, hipag and bayaw, but in the family you'll mostly call people Ate, Kuya, Tita and Tito. Many sons-in-law call their biyenan 'Mama' or 'Nanay'. Ask your wife what her family expects; they'll notice that you asked.

exercises.answer: Nakatira sa amin ang biyenan ko.

accept: kasama ko po ang asawa ko

exercises.prompt: Kuya and I were the ones who went.

lessons.title: One year, four months
lessons.intro: She just turned one, and you're on four months of leave, so people will ask about both. Numbers take a linker before a noun, the same way magandang umaga does. 'Apat buwan' needs its 'na'.

dialogue.tl: Ilang taon na si {child}?
Isang taon na po! Kaka-birthday lang po niya.
dialogue.en: One year old! She just had her birthday.

dialogue.tl: Ang bilis! Naglalakad na ba siya?
dialogue.en: So fast! Is she walking yet?

dialogue.tl: Opo! Naglalakad na po siya.
Ilang buwan kang naka-leave?
dialogue.en: How many months are you on leave?

dialogue.tl: Apat na buwan po.

grammar.title: Numbers take a linker too
grammar.explain: Before a noun, a number links like a describing word. If it ends in a vowel, add -ng: isa becomes isang taon, dalawa becomes dalawang buwan, tatlo becomes tatlong linggo, lima becomes limang araw. If it ends in a consonant, add na: apat na buwan, anim na taon. Ilan (how many) does it too: ilang taon, ilang buwan.

examples.en: I'm on leave for four months.

examples.tl: Isang buwan na lang, Pasko na!
examples.en: One more month and it's Christmas!

lessons.culture: First birthdays are big in Filipino families: a handaan (party with lots of food), pancit for long life, and gifts from ninong and ninang (godparents). Thank anyone who greets her or sends something: 'Salamat po sa regalo!' (Thank you for the gift!)

exercises.prompt: I'm on leave for four months.
accept: apat na buwan akong naka leave
apat na buwan akong naka-parental leave
naka-leave ako ng apat na buwan
naka-leave ako nang apat na buwan
naka leave ako ng apat na buwan

lessons.title: Telling the family about your days
lessons.intro: This week's patterns joined up: gusto kong + base form, pronouns in second place, and ongoing verbs, linked with kasi, pero, tapos and kaya. Aim for two-clause answers instead of 'Okay lang po'.

dialogue.tl: Kumusta ang leave mo?
Masaya po, pero medyo pagod. Gising po kasi si {child} sa gabi.
dialogue.en: Happy, but a bit tired. {child} is awake at night, you see.

dialogue.tl: Nag-aaral ka pa ba ng Tagalog?
Opo, araw-araw po. Kaya unti-unti po akong natututo.
dialogue.en: Yes, every day. So little by little I'm learning.

dialogue.tl: Ang galing mo na!

grammar.title: Joining ideas: kasi, pero, tapos, kaya
grammar.explain: Kasi gives the reason (because), kaya gives the result (so / that's why), pero gives a contrast (but), and tapos means 'and then'. Each one starts a new mini-sentence, and the usual rules still apply inside it: a pronoun goes second ('Kaya unti-unti akong natututo') and a verb after gusto stays in its base form.

examples.tl: Pagod ako kasi umiiyak siya sa gabi.
examples.en: I'm tired because she cries at night.

examples.tl: Gusto kong matuto, kaya nag-aaral ako araw-araw.
examples.en: I want to learn, so I study every day.

lessons.culture: Family talk runs on kuwento (little stories). When someone asks 'Kumusta?', one small story about her day ('Tumawa siya kanina!', she laughed earlier!) gets a much bigger reaction than 'Okay lang po'.

exercises.prompt: I'm tired because she cries at night: Pagod ako ___ umiiyak siya sa gabi.
I want to learn, so I study every day.
exercises.answer: Gusto kong matuto, kaya nag-aaral ako araw-araw.

accept: masaya ako pero medyo pagod ako
masaya po pero medyo pagod po

exercises.prompt: I'm tired because she cries at night.
exercises.answer: Pagod ako kasi umiiyak siya sa gabi.
accept: pagod ako kasi umiiyak siya sa gabi
pagod po ako kasi umiiyak siya sa gabi
pagod ako dahil umiiyak siya sa gabi
medyo pagod ako kasi umiiyak siya sa gabi
